## 1. Mutation-surface & boundary inventory

The tool is a single-invocation CLI with exactly one state-mutating operation
(the output write, §4.5) and a fixed set of external boundaries. Cycle 13
changed no mechanism — v13 is a numbers/annotation/coverage revision
(SR11-F-01..F-04) — so the inventory is unchanged from c12; the cycle's
attack surface is the NEW evidence chain v13 installs (the corrected
measured numbers and their artifacts).

| # | surface / boundary | kind | v13 status |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | argv dispatch (§4.1) | state: process exit | unchanged since D-52; pinned |
| M2 | `read_raw` input open/read (§4.2) | external: filesystem read | unchanged; E-READ |
| M3 | strict UTF-8 decode + BOM strip (§4.2) | external: none (pure) | unchanged; E-UTF8/E-EMPTY |
| M4 | parse per-record loop + FSM (§4.3) | external: none (pure) | unchanged since D-58 (c12) |
| M5 | serialize (§4.4) | external: none (pure) | unchanged since D-44 |
| M6 | write_output: encode → open → write/flush → close (§4.5) | THE mutation: output filesystem write + delete-on-failure compensation | unchanged since D-57 (c12); residues R-1/R-1b/R-4/R-5/R-6 all recorded |
| M7 | stderr single write (§4.1/§6.3) | external: channel write | unchanged; R-3 class |
| M8 | startup csv limit raise (§4.6) | process-global state at import | unchanged |
| B1 | NEW in v13: the T-C9/QC-5/D-58 measured-number chain (48c + 55h artifacts) | evidence boundary: performance claims pinned to named artifacts | the c13 attack target — see F-01 |
| B2 | NEW in v13: header probes-row annotations (SR11-F-02) | evidence boundary: live-vs-HISTORICAL citations | attacked; defects found are the spec-review twin's SR12-F-01/F-02 (cross-verified, duplicates) |

External dependencies: OS filesystem (M2/M6), process signals (M6 windows),
interpreter memory (E-MEM classes), interpreter stderr encoding (M7). No
network, no DB, no persisted state, no auth layer (N/A per §7.1 taxonomy).

## 3. Findings

### F-01 [P1|evidence-integrity/NFR-003|needs-user:false]

- **section/artifact:** §8.3 T-C9 (measured sentence), QC-5 Verification,
  §11 D-58 register row, header revision row (SR11-F-01 disposition);
  evidence artifacts appendix/48c-adv-c11-50mb.py and
  appendix/55h-sr11-fused-timing.py.
- **claim:** v13's corrected numbers present "two-quantity 27.3 s (48c) vs
  fused 9.1 s (55h)" as a same-shape, form-attributable comparison, and
  build a conforming-margin narrative on it: fused "still inside 30 s …
  leaves roughly 20 s" (QC-5), two-quantity "leaves only ~3-5 s — which is
  why D-58's fusion latitude exists" (T-C9, D-58 row).
- **evidence (live, this cycle, on this Pi 5 — the named reference-class
  host):**
  1. 48c re-run verbatim (3×): spec-shape-walk = 26.3 / 24.4 / 26.8 s —
     the ~25-27 s claim reproduces.
  2. 55h re-run verbatim: its own "48c shape" two-quantity walk = 15.0 s
     — 1.73× FASTER than 48c's number for the nominally identical loop,
     same host, same payload, same hour.
  3. 62c (interleaved, verbatim transcriptions): 48c-shape 15.1/15.0 s vs
     55h-shape 14.9/15.0 s — both ~15 s. The two artifacts' WALKS are
     algorithmically identical and agree once transcribed uniformly.
  4. 62d (root cause, deterministic): the identical loop measures
     **26.0 s at module level (48c's layout) vs 15.0 s inside a function
     (55h's layout) — 1.73×, pure CPython name-binding cost** (48c runs
     its walk at module scope; 55h wraps the same loop in a function).
  5. 62e: the binding effect (~11 s) is LARGER than the form effect
     D-58 exists to address (~6 s): the FUSED walk at module level
     measures **19.6 s — 2.2× the spec's "9.1 s fused walk" claim**.
  6. 62b (end-to-end, matched binding): fused pipeline 10.2 s,
     two-quantity 16.0 s — both far inside 30 s; the "leaves only ~3-5 s"
     margin story holds at NO consistent binding on the reference host
     (the 3-5 s residue exists only by mixing 48c's module-level walk
     number with 55h's function-local stage numbers).
- **minimal counterexample:** Run `python3 appendix/48c-adv-c11-50mb.py`
  (prints spec-shape-walk=24-27 s) and `python3
  appendix/55h-sr11-fused-timing.py` (prints TWO-QUANTITY=15.0 s) on the
  same reference-class host back to back. Both numbers are now normative
  spec citations for the SAME quantity (the §4.3.2+§4.3.3 walk), and they
  disagree by 1.73×. Per T-C9's own sentence the two-quantity form "is
  also conforming" — but an implementor who writes the conforming
  two-quantity parse as a FUNCTION (the natural reading of §2.2's stage
  functions; 15 s) and an implementor who writes it at module level (26 s)
  get a 2× spread on a diagnostic the spec narrates to a ~3-5 s margin.
  The number v13 just corrected is itself an artifact of measurement
  regime, not of the form it is attributed to.
- **impact:** D-58's recorded rationale ("the literal two-pass walk
  consumed 27.3 s … making T-C9 flap on the documented floor hardware")
  misattributes a binding effect to the form; the conforming-form margin
  guidance ("~20 s left" vs "only ~3-5 s left") is not derivable from any
  single consistent measurement; a future cold auditor re-running the two
  named artifacts gets a 1.73× contradiction between two normative
  citations, the exact SR11-F-01 defect class (authoritative artifacts
  disagree) at one severity lower — but this time installed BY the fix.
- **required disposition:** one binding-controlled measurement set: either
  (a) re-measure both forms inside functions (or both at module level) in
  ONE probe and cite only those numbers (expected ≈15 s vs ≈9-10 s
  function-bound, ≈26 s vs ≈20 s module-bound — fused stays ahead at
  either binding, which is the honest support for D-58), and state the
  binding in the T-C9 sentence; or (b) drop the per-form margin narrative
  and keep only the envelope outcome assertion (T-C9's own "diagnostic
  spot check" framing, per REQ NFR-003's "spot check, not a hard gate").
  The 27.3 s / "~3-5 s" pair should stop being normative either way.
- **decision owner:** spec-designer.
- **verification required:** re-aim of the T-C9/QC-5/D-58 text pins
  (58-rev13 P-series) after the fold; one new binding-controlled timing
  probe cited in the header probes row.

### F-02 [P2|evidence-integrity/D-58|needs-user:false]

- **section/artifact:** §4.3.3 CONFORMING FUSION paragraph and §11 D-58
  row ("outcome-identical … opening line M"), citing appendix/51 B3;
  appendix/55h (which the D-58 row now also cites as timing evidence).
- **claim:** the fused and two-quantity forms produce IDENTICAL
  observables including "opening line M".
- **evidence:** appendix/51 B3's `two_pass_span`/`fused_span` latch
  `opening` at the FIRST FIELD_START→QUOTED transition (`if st == 2 and
  opening is None`). For any record whose FIRST quoted field closes and a
  LATER field's quote is the unclosed one, that is not the quote §4.3.3
  normatively reports: the spec's own worked case `h1,h2\n"a\r\nb",c,"d\ne`
  has first-field quote on record-relative line 1, unclosed third-field
  quote on record-relative line 2, and T-C7/S-10 pin M = 2 + 2 − 1 = 3.
  B3 still passes because it asserts only tuple-identity BETWEEN the two
  shapes (both compute the same wrong-for-this-purpose opening), not
  identity with the normative M; 55h's walk prints uq=(2, 2) — M=2 — for
  this exact corpus, live, where the spec pins M=3. So B3 is valid for
  "the two shapes agree with each other" and void as evidence for "M is an
  outcome-identical observable" in the multi-quote case; the D-58 row's
  "live: appendix/51 B3 over CRLF/CR/quote corpora" overstates what B3
  computes. The normative SPEC text is not wrong (M is pinned correctly by
  T-U3/T-C7); the defect is the evidence citation.
- **minimal counterexample:** input `h1,h2\n"a\r\nb",c,"d\ne`: spec §4.3.3
  worked case requires E-UQ with N=2, M=3. Run 55h (or B3's spans) on it:
  both compute the opening at the FIRST quote (record-relative line 1) →
  M=2. The cited "outcome-identity" probes would bless a build reporting
  M=2 — non-conforming against T-C7 — as identical to a correct build.
- **impact:** bounded — an implementor copying 55h/B3's first-quote latch
  into a real build produces wrong M on multi-quote records and the cited
  probes stay green; the defect hides behind probe validity, not spec
  text.
- **required disposition:** either re-aim the D-58/B3 evidence cite to a
  probe whose opening-line observable is the UNCLOSED quote's line (and
  add the multi-quote corpus with M asserted = 3), or scope the cite to
  what B3 proves (per-record break count and end-state identity) and name
  T-U3/T-C7 as the M authority. Register-row wording fix on the next
  designer touch.
- **decision owner:** spec-designer.
- **verification required:** new/re-aimed identity probe with the
  multi-quote corpus asserting M; text-pin re-run.

duplicate/double-submission, retry-after-partial-success, concurrent
execution, partial failure at every async boundary of M6,
timeout/cancellation (single-KI, double-KI, at-open), crash mid-op,
